question_sources.actor_role: Robert De Niro — James "Jimmy the Gent" Conway

sources.title: AFI Catalog: Goodfellas (1990)
supports: Robert De Niro is credited as James ‘Jimmy the Gent’ Conway.
The film was adapted from Nicholas Pileggi’s Wiseguy and its title changed to avoid confusion with the television drama Wiseguy.
AFI records De Niro recommending himself for the Conway role and describes the Copacabana tracking-shot staging.
sources.limits: AFI records a dramatic film’s credits and production history. Its ‘based on a true story’ opening and end-card wording are not a complete historical account of people or events.

sources.organization: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences
sources.title: The 63rd Academy Awards (1991)
supports: Good Fellas received six nominations and one win.
Joe Pesci won Actor in a Supporting Role for the film.
The ledger lists Good Fellas nominations for Bracco, Scorsese, Schoonmaker, Winkler, Pileggi, and Scorsese.
sources.limits: This awards ledger supports category outcomes, not the film’s plot or real-world historical accuracy. It does not award De Niro for playing Conway.

sources.title: AFI Catalog: Scarface (1983)
supports: Al Pacino is credited as Tony Montana; Brian De Palma directed and Oliver Stone wrote the 1983 film.
The 1983 film reworks the 1932 film’s ‘The World Is Yours’ motif for Tony Montana.
The final credits describe Scarface as fictional and say its characters do not represent the Cuban-American community.
AFI records the MPAA rating appeal that resulted in an R rating.
sources.limits: The page supports film credits, production/reception history, and the film’s own disclaimer; it is not evidence that the story documents actual Cuban-American lives or the drug trade.

sources.title: AFI Catalog: Scarface (1932)
supports: The earlier Scarface is a 1932 Howard Hawks film starring Paul Muni and based on Armitage Trail’s 1930 novel.
AFI explicitly identifies the 1983 film as another Scarface released by Universal, directed by De Palma and written by Stone, with Pacino among its stars.
This distinguishes Pacino’s Tony Montana in the 1983 remake from Tony Camonte in the 1932 film.
sources.limits: This record establishes adaptation lineage and the separate films; it does not make the 1983 fictional narrative a documentary account of criminal history.
